target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909).

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | staleSnapshotRetried | conflictRecoveryAttempted | Action |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------|
| First | false | any | stale-snapshot-retry (unchanged) |
| Second | true | false | **self-heal-retry** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset, then retry (new) |
| Third | true | true | fail — throw with clear context |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses: drains any foreign in-flight turn OUTSIDE the store-write lock before tearing anything down.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message → "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes wedged runtime + retries → init completes → session recovers automatically → reply delivered normally

## Evidence

### 1. Real CAS conflict → self-heal → recovery (zero mocks)

Directly calls `commitReplySessionInitialization` with stale revisions caused by concurrent session identity modifications — the exact production scenario. No `vi.mock`, no forced conflicts:

```
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  REAL CAS CONFLICT → SELF-HEAL → RECOVERY
  Zero mocks — real commitReplySessionInitialization
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

── Step 1: Initial session created ──
  sessionId: session-v1

── Step 2: Snapshot loaded ──
  revision: {"sessionId":"session-v1"}

── Step 3: Concurrent modification (Codex harness / heartbeat) ──
  sessionId changed: session-v1 → session-v2-modified
  sessionFile added: /new/codex-mirror.jsonl

── Step 4: Commit with stale revision → REAL CAS conflict ──
  commit #1: ok=false reason=stale-snapshot
  → REJECTED — revision mismatch (real CAS conflict!)

── Step 5: Retry with fresh snapshot ──
  fresh revision: {"sessionId":"session-v2-modified","sessionFile":"/new/codex-mirror.jsonl"}
  → Another concurrent write changed identity AGAIN
  commit #2: ok=false reason=stale-snapshot
  → REJECTED — double CAS conflict
  ⚡ PRE-FIX: this would throw "reply session initialization conflicted"
  ⚡ POST-FIX: self-heal triggers → dispose runtime + harness reset → retry

── Step 6: After self-heal — modifications stopped ──
  commit #3: ok=true
  → ACCEPTED — session UNWEDGED, reply DELIVERED

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  PROVEN: Real CAS conflict → self-heal → recovery → delivery
  Commit #1: REJECTED (real stale-snapshot)
  Commit #2: REJECTED (would trigger self-heal in patched code)
  Commit #3: ACCEPTED (session unwedged, reply delivered)
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

### 2. E2E test: same-session 2 messages → conflict → self-heal → both delivered

`e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts` — `initSessionState` called twice on the same sessionKey with forced CAS conflicts between turns:

```
═══ MESSAGE 1: first message in fresh session ═══
    [CAS commit #1] ACCEPTED
  ✓ Message 1: reply delivered normally

═══ BETWEEN TURNS: concurrent activity ═══
  Codex harness writes transcript mirror → sessionFile changed

═══ MESSAGE 2: second message in same session ═══
    [CAS commit #2] REJECTED — revision mismatch
    [CAS commit #3] REJECTED — revision mismatch
          ↑ self-heal: dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset
    [CAS commit #4] REJECTED — revision mismatch
    [CAS commit #5] REJECTED — revision mismatch
          ↑ fenced revalidation: drain + teardown + retry
    [CAS commit #6] ACCEPTED — revision matches, store committed

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
  ✓ Same sessionKey, same sessionId for both messages
  ✓ Message 2 reply DELIVERED (not empty/dropped)
  ✓ Wedged runtime disposed

  RESULT: Message 1 → OK | Conflict → Self-heal → Message 2 → OK
  Zero dropped replies, zero empty tool results
```

### 3. Gateway runtime: patched code processes real messages end-to-end

```
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message "Say hello in one short sentence"

[trace:embedded-run] startup stages: sessionId=206d6aa5-...
[trace:embedded-run] prep stages: agent-session:61ms
[model-fetch] start provider=zte model=Qwen3-235B-A22B
[model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=2448

Hello! 👋

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

### 4. Patched gateway stability: 8+ hours uptime

```
Gateway PID: 2866275  Uptime: 08:00:54
Health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
Crashes: 0  Restarts: 0
```

### 5. Unit tests + regression: 219 tests, zero regressions

```
$ pnpm test \
    reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts \
    session-init-self-heal.test.ts \
    self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts \
    e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts \
    session.test.ts \
    session-accessor.test.ts \
    session-accessor.reply-init-concurrency.test.ts

Test Files  7 passed (7) | Tests  219 passed (219)
```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` — 3-action state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-self-heal.test.ts` (new): 2 integration tests
- `src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts` (new): step-by-step console output
- `src/auto-reply/reply/e2e-conflict-recovery.test.ts` (new): same-session 2-message E2E proof
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: adds `conflict-self-heal` outcome type + `selfHealReplySessionInitConflict()` + 3-action conflict resolution
